purpose: Testosterone enanthate is used to treat men whose bodies do not make enough testosterone on their own, a condition called hypogonadism. It is also used in some transgender men as part of hormone therapy. In some cases, doctors may prescribe it for delayed puberty in teenage boys.
how_it_works: Testosterone is the main male hormone your body naturally produces. This medication works by replacing or adding testosterone that your body is not making in sufficient amounts. It is given as an injection and slowly releases testosterone into your bloodstream over one to two weeks, helping your body maintain normal hormone levels.
common_side_effects: Pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site; acne or oily skin; increased facial or body hair; mood changes or irritability; higher red blood cell count; decreased sperm production; fluid retention or mild swelling in the ankles or feet.
warnings: This medication should not be used to enhance athletic performance or build muscle, as misuse can be dangerous. It can increase your risk of blood clots, heart attack, or stroke. It may cause liver problems with long-term use. Women who are pregnant should never handle this medication, as it can harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor if you have heart disease, liver or kidney problems, enlarged prostate, or sleep apnea before starting this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 50 to 400 mg injected into a muscle every 2 to 4 weeks, depending on your condition and how your body responds. Your doctor will determine the exact dose and schedule that is right for you. Never adjust your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
